Where you *shouldn't* lean on me: anything involving messy non-integer amounts, long chains of dependent calculations, or sorting/ranking tasks — treat those as different jobs. Honestly? Treat it like any volunteer's figures and verify every line. That's not a knock on the capability — multiplication is genuinely where I'm strongest, and I'd expect far fewer slips than a tired volunteer on a long evening. But "most of the time right" is exactly the trap in bookkeeping: occasional errors are the ones that hide, because everyone relaxes after a good streak. An uneven tool is more dangerous than a uniformly mediocre one, precisely because it earns trust it hasn't fully earned.

The good news is that your workflow doesn't change much. A second check on machine-generated numbers is usually fast — the first pass being solid means verification is confirmation rather than correction. So: let me do the heavy lifting, keep the double-check discipline anyway, and your treasurer's meetings stay boring in the best way.
